judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short cross-reference to Section 2.02(b).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.02(b) (c215) makes Tranche B available only after Financial Closure, a condition this definition does not signal but does not contradict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed dollar amount.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Together with Tranche A's US$150,000,000 it equals the Total Commitment (c199).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list runs together ungrammatically — 'all proceeds from any Equity Interest proceeds, insurance, expropriation the proceeds of the sale of assets and other proceeds and amounts' — leaving the class of deposits genuinely unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Escrow Account definition (c070) already requires 'all Cash and receivables ... or payments otherwise received by Borrower' to be deposited in a different account, so the two accounts claim the same proceeds.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Names a specific firm with an open successor formula ('such other independent, professional and reputable insurance advisory firm appointed').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits within 'Consultants' (c044) and Sections 4.01(j)/5.07(b), which are outside the reproduced text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'in the ordinary course of the Borrower's business' is a soft limit but the rest is specific as to lender type and purpose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a permitted debt basket keyed to Section 6.01, which is not reproduced.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The appointment mechanics ('appointed by the Lenders ... and acceptable to the Borrower and the Upstream Supplier Financing Creditors which are parties to such Intercreditor Agreement at such time') are conditional on an agreement that may never exist.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Agents' (c015) treats the Intercreditor Agent as an existing party, while c107 makes the Intercreditor Agreement itself contingent and c040 says a Common Project Financing Facility 'may' be subject to one.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'in form and substance satisfactory to the Borrower and the Required Lenders' and the trailing 'if and when appointed' leave the agreement's existence and content entirely undetermined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Supplier Financing' (c185) states the Supplier Financing 'shall be subject to an Intercreditor Agreement' as a firm requirement, whereas c040 and c106 treat such an agreement as optional and contingent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Calling it 'the one-time request' is in tension with the plural 'Interest Periods' in the same sentence and with the section heading 'Interest Elections'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.07(b) (c233) requires the election to be made in the first Borrowing Request, yet Section 2.07(c) (c234) has the Facility Agent advising Lenders of the Interest Period 'for each Borrowing', so whether elections recur is genuinely unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single fixed percentage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used in Section 2.06(h) (c230) and the interest provisions consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defined only by reference to Eurodollar Rate Borrowings, so it supplies no payment date for interest accruing at any alternate rate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.04 (c222) expressly contemplates funding 'at a different rate of interest' under Section 2.14, and Section 2.06(h) prescribes interim interest payable on demand, leaving a gap this definition does not fill.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumeration runs '(i) ... and (iii)' with no clause (ii), the provisos then restart the lettering '(a), (b), (c)' after clauses (a) and (b) of the definition itself, and the closing sentence refers to 'the most recent conversion or continuation of such Borrowing' although the Agreement provides no conversion or continuation mechanic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.07(a) (c232) repeats the same defective '(i)/(iii)' enumeration, and Section 2.03(c) fixes every Borrowing as a Eurodollar Rate Borrowing, so the conversion/continuation language has no counterpart anywhere in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but conventionally structured definition with an express valuation rule for non-cash transfers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to a Person becoming a 'Subsidiary', though c183 records that the Borrower has none and Section 5.12 restricts subsidiaries.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'each other Lender designated by the Borrower' makes the class of Issuing Banks unilaterally expandable, and the Affiliate limb ('in its discretion but with the consent of Borrower') sits awkwardly with it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.06(e) (c227) makes the conversion of LC Disbursements turn on whether the Issuing Bank is itself a Lender or an Affiliate of one, so the elasticity of this definition has direct operative consequences.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical '(including any additional Issuing Bank pursuant to which a Lender agrees to act as an Issuing Bank)' is grammatically incoherent — a bank is not something 'pursuant to which' a party agrees to act.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.06(b) (c225) and 2.06(f) allow an Issuing Bank to use its own standard form 'as accepted by the Borrower', so the priority between Exhibit C and a bank's form is left to negotiation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short and specific definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.06(e), (g) and (h).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (b) opens 'the sum of (i) ... plus the aggregate amount of all LC Disbursements' with no clause (ii), a numbering failure in a formula that determines exposure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Borrowing' (c021) treats an LC Exposure as a Borrowing and 'Unused Commitment' (c204) subtracts LC Exposure, so the mis-enumerated arithmetic feeds directly into the availability tests in Sections 2.06(a) and (b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The last limb speaks of an assignee 'that becomes a Project Lender pursuant to an Assignment and Assumption', importing a Recital-defined term into the operative definition of Lender.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Project Lender' (c161) is defined only by the Recitals and there sweeps in supplier-credit providers, so an assignee could be a Lender without being a Project Lender in the Recital sense, or vice versa.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard two-limb fund and affiliate definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used in the assignment provisions; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing words 'on the same terms as the required by the Loans' are ungrammatical, and the conditional 'if and to the extent' clause leaves it unclear whether the denominator shrinks when the other creditors do not require prepayment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the mirror of c009 and c206 but keys to Section 2.11(b) rather than 2.11(f), and Section 2.11 is not part of the reproduced instrument, so the three pro rata formulas cannot be reconciled from the text available.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence that bundles an instrument description ('usance, sight or advance'), an issuance deadline, an expiry test, four numbered operational conditions and a negotiation deadline; the syntax makes it hard to tell which limits are definitional and which are conditions of issuance.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Four years from the 29 December 2010 date of the Agreement is 29 December 2014, yet the same definition allows negotiation of a letter of credit until 30 December 2014, and the LC issuance window (to 30 June 2013) outruns nothing while the Term Loan Availability Period ends 30 September 2013 even though LC Disbursements automatically convert into Term Loans under Section 2.06(e).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure back-reference to the Recitals.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It makes a recital operative, and the Recitals describe the Letter of Credit Facility without any stated size, unlike the Term Loan Facility.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The fallback sentence begins 'In the event that such rate is not available at the time of determination for any other Interest Period for any reason', where the word 'other' has no antecedent and appears to narrow the fallback unintentionally.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It identifies the source as the Reuters 'LIBOR01' screen while 'Market Disruption Event' (c129) refers to the Reuters 'LIBO01' screen, and Section 2.14's alternate-rate machinery depends on which screen governs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional two-limb security-interest definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 'Permitted Encumbrances' (c151) and 'Collateral' (c036).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A form-referential definition fixing a precise 51% pledge; 'reasonably satisfactory' to four different parties is the only soft element.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interlocks with 'Pledged Borrower LLC Interests' (c158) and with the 49% Change in Control threshold (c033), which together leave only a two-point margin.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list closing with 'any other document designated from time to time as a Loan Document by the Lenders or the Facility Agent' — a unilaterally expandable catch-all appended to specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because 'Obligations' (c142) and 'Security Documents' (c178) are defined by reference to the Loan Documents, the unilateral designation power can enlarge the secured perimeter without the Borrower's agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Term Loan' (c191) says a Term Loan is a Loan made pursuant to Section 2.06 or 2.01, which is consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list includes 'deferred payment guaranties, shortfall undertakings or payment undertakings or any nature whatsoever', a garbled phrase (evidently 'of any nature') that leaves the class unbounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It excludes Unsecured Subordinated Promoter Loans and Working Capital Bank Financing, mirroring 'Short-Term Debt' (c179) and 'Total Debt' (c200), which apply the same exclusions again — a real double-counting risk despite the 'without duplications' language in c200.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A naming definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the preamble; no arranger duties appear in the reproduced text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Each limb turns on what 'Required Lenders determine', including the wholly subjective limb (iv) that deposits 'are not available to such Required Lenders'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Limb (ii) refers to the Reuters 'LIBO01' screen while the LIBO Rate definition (c122) uses the Reuters 'LIBOR01' screen, and the Reference Banks fallback here does not match the Facility Agent quotation fallback there.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'material adverse effect on ... the business, financial condition, operations or performance or properties of the Borrower since March 31, 2010' is both vague and grammatically odd — the 'since' clause is grafted onto a noun list rather than a change concept.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same phrase does heavy work in c012(7), c013(m) and c198, which carve out capital contributions made in respect of litigation 'that would reasonably be expected to result in a Material Adverse Effect', so its vagueness propagates into the financial definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'including those listed in Schedule 4.01(f) and including, but not limited to, environmental permits, rights for developing mines ... or a mining plan, if required' piles a non-exhaustive list on a schedule and closes with a conditional 'if required'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It underpins conditions precedent in Article IV that are not reproduced; nothing in the available text conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference to another document's definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The LLC Pledge Agreement (c124) is not part of the reproduced instrument, so the content is external but not inconsistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies a specific agreement and its amendments and related documents by date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly preserved as a Permitted Encumbrance under c151(q), which is coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A naming definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used in c154 consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short instrument definition with a 'reasonably satisfactory in form and substance' standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 'Mortgaged Property' (c136) and 'Security Documents' (c178).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is partly circular — Mortgaged Property is property 'with respect to which a Mortgage is to be granted' and then 'includes (i) each other parcel ... with respect to which a Mortgage is granted' — and limb (ii) conditions mining rights on obtaining third-party acknowledgments.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Collateral' (c036) says it 'shall also include the Mortgaged Properties', so any indeterminacy here directly affects the collateral perimeter, and 'Additional Collateral Date' (c007) turns on acquisitions of 'material' property.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statutory cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the other ERISA definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The arithmetic is broken: '(A) ... minus, (B) ... and (C) minus mark-to-market amounts ... that, individually or in the aggregate, are less than twenty five million Dollars', which leaves both the sign of clause (C) and the effect of the US$25,000,000 test genuinely unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It draws on 'Indebtedness permitted in Section 6.01' and on the DSRA, Escrow Account and Unrestricted Account, the last of which is never separately defined in the reproduced text (it appears only in c138, c155 and c203).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Total Assets minus Total Debt' calls the result 'Net Equity' even though Total Debt (c200) is narrower than total liabilities, so the label does not match the arithmetic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Total Assets (c198) already strips out litigation-related capital contributions and Total Debt strips out Unsecured Subordinated Promoter Loans, so the same items are adjusted twice in computing this measure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long aggregation clause with a no-double-counting opener; broad but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It differs from 'Cash Sweep Net Finance Charges' (c032) only in the debt to which it applies, which invites mismatch between the DSCR and Cash Sweep DSCR tests.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An elaborate netting formula with nested lettering; each deduction is specific, though 'reasonably estimated to be payable ... as determined reasonably and in good faith by a Financial Officer' leaves discretion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to taxes 'in the case of any such event in respect of any Foreign Subsidiary', although c183 records that the Borrower has no Subsidiary at all — leftover form language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional payment-and-performance definition; the closing limiter 'in each case to the extent arising in connection with the Obligations' is circular but standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is folded into 'Secured Obligations' (c174) with the Additional Obligations (c010) and used in Section 2.06(j); coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any of the Borrowers' is plural although the Agreement defines a single Borrower, and the sentence uses 'any of' with a two-item class.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same plural residue appears in the Foreign Lender definition (c085) and Section 2.06(b) ('a Borrower shall hand deliver'), suggesting an unconverted multi-borrower form running through the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'each of the operative contracts and agreements entered into by the Borrower for the sale of goods and products produced by the Project' is broad, and the exclusion turns on a 45-day payment term that is easy to structure around.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Project Contract' (c160) carves Offtake Contracts and Agreements out of its Contract Threshold relief, so every Offtake Contract requires a Consent and Agreement (c042) regardless of size — a significant consequence riding on this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of tax types closing with 'or similar taxes, charges or levies', a modest catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mutually exclusive with 'Excluded Taxes' (c075) and 'Indemnified Taxes' (c097).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A back-reference to the Recitals identifying a named company.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c090, c091 and c124.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.04(c) is not reproduced; no visible conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statutory citation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only in Section 9.15.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statutory body definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the ERISA definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'de-bottlenecking and other similar performance and operational and efficiency enhancing modifications' is a vague class dressed up as a specific one, and the annual cap applies to an 'aggregate amount' without saying whether it is incurrence or outstanding.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Permitted Project Change' (c155) uses the same phrase but treats such modifications as exempt from Required Lender consent only when funded from equity or the Unrestricted Account, while this definition assumes they may be debt-funded up to US$50,000,000 a year.
